fn-36E60.mechanism: Saves PR and calls the routine at 0x00022CF4. It zero-extends the low byte of the return value in r0. If that byte equals 1, it loads the float at ROM 0x000CC288 into fr8. Net effect: both 0xFFFF7A20 and 0xFFFF7A38 receive the same one of two ROM float constants. Which one depends on whether the 0x22CF4 routine returned 1. The two instructions after rts (mov.l r13/r14 pushes) belong to the next function.
fn-36E60.purpose: unknown. The function picks one of two calibration floats from a boolean or mode condition and writes it to two RAM variables, likely an active value and a copy or initial value. What the condition and the constants mean cannot be told from this code.

The second byte is a bit mask. 3) Loads the RAM byte at 0xFFFFADAC+offset, ANDs it with the mask, and sets r2=1 if the result is nonzero (cmp/pl; the result can only be 0..255) or 0 otherwise. 4) Pushes 0 as a fifth, stack-passed argument. fn-0CBAC.mechanism: Increments the byte counter at 0xFFFF447A on every call. It then re-reads the counter, zero-extends it and compares it with 4. If the counter is below 4 the function simply returns. Once it reaches 4 or more, it writes 0 back to 0xFFFF447A. It then calls the subroutine at 0x00CA72 eight times, passing an index in r4 each time (set in the bsr delay slots): 0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 9, 10 and finally 12. The last call is a tail call: it uses bra, with the pr restore in the delay slot. Everything after 0x00CBEC is literal pool or the start of the next function (0x00CC1C begins another routine with register saves) and is ignored.

These are likely channel or slot numbers in some table, such as sensor or ADC channels, but what the indices mean and what 0x00CA72 does cannot be told from this code. The exact purpose is unknown.

fn-6F114.mechanism: Works on a byte block at 0xFFFF96A4: [0] and [1] are enable flags, [2] is a counter and [3] is an armed flag. If byte[0]!=1 or byte[1]!=1, it clears [2] and [3] and returns. Status==2: it compares counter [2] (unsigned) with the calibration byte at ROM 0xD8A40. If counter >= threshold it tail-calls 0x9ED90 with r4=1, and the counter is not reset. If below, it sets [2] = uint8_add_sat([2],1). Status==1: it sets [2]=0 and tail-calls 0x9EDEC with r4=1. Any other status: it sets [2]=0 and returns.

When the enable conditions hold and the monitored input reports state 2 (probably abnormal), it counts up to a calibrated limit and then reports a fault through 0x9ED90. When the input reports state 1 (probably normal), it clears the count and reports a pass through 0x9EDEC. The argument r4=1 probably picks the DTC or monitor index. Which fault is monitored cannot be told from this code.

fn-459F6.mechanism: Reads three floats: fr5 from 0xFFFF7F4C, fr4 from engine_load_current (0xFFFF63F8) and fr9 from 0xFFFF3234. It also reads fr14 from 0xFFFF8258 (0xFFFF8268 - 16). The multiply fr14 = [0xFFFF8258] * [0xFFFF3234] sits in the branch delay slot, so it always runs. It then tests the ROM byte at 0x000D299B. If that byte is zero, it jumps straight to the end. If it is non-zero, it calls table_lookup_2D with r4 = 0x000AE6B8 (table descriptor). The inputs appear to be fr4 = engine load and fr5 = [0xFFFF7F4C]. The lookup result is stored at 0xFFFF8268. That result is multiplied by [0xFFFF8200], the product is stored at 0xFFFF8264, and it is added to fr14. In both paths fr14 is finally stored to 0xFFFF8260. So [8260] = [8258]*[3234] + (flag ? table(load, [7F4C]) * [8200] : 0). When the flag is zero, 0xFFFF8268 and 0xFFFF8264 are left unchanged (stale or initial values). fr14 and pr are saved and restored.

The pattern is consistent with a Subaru ignition-timing build-up: base x factor + knock-advance map(load, RPM) x IAM-style multiplier [0xFFFF8200], enabled by a calibration flag. This is not confirmed by the code.

The ROM byte at 0x000D299B is a calibration enable gating the table term.

fn-06738.mechanism: Saves pr and makes 8 bytes of stack. Calls critical_section_enter twice with r5=0xE0, saving the two returned tokens at @(4,r15) and @r15. It then works on four byte-wide peripheral registers, all reached through sign-extended mov.w literals (0xF0xx -> 0xFFFFF0xx), and writes each one only if it is not already in the wanted state. (1) 0xFFFFF018: if it is not 0x80, write 0x80. (2) 0xFFFFF01A: if (val & 3) != 0, write val & 0xFC, which clears bits 1:0. (3) 0xFFFFF01E: if bit 3 is clear, write 0xFA. (4) 0xFFFFF019: if it is not 6, write 6. Finally it calls critical_section_exit twice with the saved tokens, in reverse order, restores the stack and returns. Nothing is computed and no RAM is touched.
fn-06738.purpose: This is most likely an idempotent setup or refresh of one SH7058 SCI channel, probably SCI3 at base 0xFFFFF018, for clocked-synchronous serial with internal clock and MSB-first bit order. In that reading: SMR3=0x80 selects C/A=1 (clocked synchronous, 8-bit, CKS=00). Clearing SCR3 CKE1:0 selects the internal clock with SCK output. SDCR3=0xFA, the reset value 0xF2 plus DIR, gives MSB-first. BRR3=6 sets the bit rate. It is run with interrupts masked so the reconfiguration is atomic. The use of a synchronous serial link to an external chip is a hunch; a serial EEPROM is a plausible candidate.
evidence: Literal 0xF018 is loaded with mov.w and sign-extends to 0xFFFFF018; the other addresses are 0xFFFFF019, 0xFFFFF01A and 0xFFFFF01E, all at offsets +0, +1, +2 and +6 from one base.
In the SH7058 SCI register layout each channel takes 8 bytes from 0xFFFFF000 (SMR, BRR, SCR, TDR, SSR, RDR, SDCR at +0..+6). That places this base at SCI channel 3.
Value 0x80 written to the +0 register matches SMR with C/A=1 (synchronous mode). The AND with 0xFC on the +2 register matches clearing SCR CKE1/CKE0.
The +6 register is tested for bit 3 and written 0xFA (0xF2|0x08), which matches the SDCR DIR bit (MSB-first) on top of its reset value 0xF2.
The +1 register is forced to 6, which fits a BRR bit-rate value.
Every write is conditional (compare first, write only if different), the pattern of a periodic 'ensure configuration' routine.
The whole sequence is wrapped in two nested critical_section_enter(0xE0)/critical_section_exit pairs.
fn-06738.weakest_link: The mapping of 0xFFFFF018-0xFFFFF01E to SCI3 SMR/BRR/SCR/SDCR comes from recalled SH7058 hardware-manual layout, not from anything in this listing. The device on the other end of the link is not visible here.

Two short stretches of this sequence are wrapped by a call to 0x317C with r4=16, whose return value is saved on the stack, and a later call to 0x3190 with that saved value in r4. The first wraps 0x56AAA; the second wraps 0x7E2D8. In the middle of the list, 0x5AB44 is called with r4=1. (2) Value 0xFF: runs a short sequence: 0x21F66, 0x24D30, 0x5AB44(r4=0), 0x267D4, 0x9E1CA, then tail-jumps to 0xA67D6. (3) Any other nonzero value: only tail-calls 0x5AB44 with r4=1. The 0x317C/0x3190 pairs are probably a save-SR/raise-interrupt-mask and restore critical section around routines that need atomic access.

fn-3684A.mechanism: GBR is set to 0xFFFF798C and r13 to 0xFFFF79F8; the slots below are offsets from r13. (1) It reads rpm_current (fr12), engine_load_current (fr15) and the previous product at 0xFFFF79AC (fr14). (2) It stores 0xFFFF79B4 = [FFFF7F48] + [FFFF8258] - [FFFF7E90]. (3) It calls float_deadband_check on [FFFF798C] with 0.0 and the constant at 0x036A34. If the result is non-zero it uses the 2D map 0xAD960 and the 1D table 0xAC5F8; otherwise it uses the 2D map 0xAD97C and the 1D table 0xAC60C. The 2D map is read at (load, rpm) into 0xFFFF79D4, and the 1D table at the 79B4 sum into 0xFFFF79D8. (4) It stores the new raw value 0xFFFF79AC = 79D4 * 79D8. (5) It chooses a coefficient map with hysteresis and keeps the pointer at 0xFFFF79F8 (GBR+108). If the new value is above old + [CC224] the pointer becomes 0xAD998. If |new - old| > [CC224] and new < old - [CC224] it becomes 0xAD9B4. Otherwise the previous pointer is kept. (6) It looks up the chosen map at (load, rpm) into 0xFFFF79B0. It then sets 0xFFFF79A4 = float_lag_filter(input = 79AC, state = 79A4, coefficient = 79B0, fr7 = constant at 0x036A64). (7) It looks up the 2D map 0xAD9D0 at (load, rpm) into 0xFFFF79DC. It then sets 0xFFFF79A8 = float_lag_filter(input = 79A4, state = 79A8, coefficient = 79DC, same constant). The result is a two-stage cascaded first-order filter with a different first-stage coefficient when the raw value is rising than when it is falling.
fn-3684A.purpose: Unknown. The code computes a modelled quantity: an rpm/load base map scaled by a correction looked up from a sum/difference of three other RAM values. The value is then smoothed through two lag stages, with separate rise and fall rates. The float_deadband_check result on 0xFFFF798C selects between two map/table pairs (0xAD960/0xAC5F8 vs 0xAD97C/0xAC60C)

GBR is set to the 0xFFFF7450 flag block. The function reads ect_current, ect_gated_c and rpm_current, plus floats at 6898, 620C, 77DC, 7BA8, 7800, 77C0 and 77C8. It also reads word 67EC and bytes 7828, 7829, 72A1, A56B and ACF0, and calls three helpers (22F92, 29BA4, 1CF46). The float at 653C is loaded but immediately overwritten, so it is unused.
(1) Hysteresis flags: [+8]=1 when (6898-620C)<=K_CBE68 and 0 when it exceeds K_CBE6C. [+13]=1 when rpm<=K_CBE70 and 0 when rpm>K_CBE74. [+14]=1 when table_1D(AD458, rpm)<=620C and 0 when (table-K_CBEA0)>620C. [+15]=0 when 77C0<K_CBE8C and 1 when 77C0>=K_CBE90. [+16]=1 when 77C0<K_CBE94 and 0 when 77C0>=K_CBE98.
(2) Edge counters saturating at byte K_CBBD6. [+11] is reset on a 1->0 transition of byte A56B (previous value kept in [+9]); otherwise it counts up. [+12] is reset on a 0->1 transition of byte ACF0 (previous value kept in [+10]); otherwise it counts up. r11=1 only when both counters have reached the limit.
(3) r14=1 when byte 7828==0, or when [+15] and [+16] are both 1.
(4) If helper 1CF46 returns 1, outputs [+0],[+1],[+2],[+3] are all cleared. Otherwise:
- [+4]=sub_3160E(ect_gated, byte 72A1).
- [+6]=uint16 table ACE00(ect_gated).
- Base enable r6 requires all of: ect_current>=K_CBE64; word 67EC >= [+4] if byte 7829==0, or >= [+6] if it is 1; both float_deadband_check calls on 798C and 7A20 return 0; byte 7D18==0; 77C8>K_CBEA4.
- r1 = ([+8] or [+13] or [+14]) and result of 22F92 !=1 and byte 7464==0.
(5) Outputs:
- [+0] = r6 and 22F92 result !=1 and 7828==0.
- [+1] = r6 and r1 and 7828==0.
- [+2] = r6 and r1 and 7BA8<K_CBE78 and byte 7BB0==0 and r11 and r14.
- [+3] = r6 and r1 and 7BA8<K_CBE78 and K_CBE7C<=77DC<K_CBE80 and K_CBE84<=7800<K_CBE88 and r11.
fn-3162C.purpose: Most likely the enable-condition evaluator for a group of OBD diagnostic monitors. Four monitor-permission bytes (7450..7453) are produced from coolant temperature (including a minimum time-after-start that depends on coolant temperature), low rpm / idle-like conditions, settling counters after switch transitions, and other gates. Which monitor these enables serve is unknown from this code alone.
evidence: Outputs are 0/1 bytes written to GBR 7450+0..3 that are ANDs of many conditions: the classic enable-flag pattern.
Hysteresis pairs (two calibration thresholds per signal) on rpm_current, on the difference 6898-620C, on a table of rpm vs 620C, and on 77C0.

A word counter 67EC is compared against thresholds derived from ect_gated_c via table ACE00 or sub_3160E. The selection by byte 7829 suggests a time-since-start or elapsed-time requirement that depends on coolant temperature.
A minimum coolant temperature check: ect_current>=K_CBE64.
Edge-reset counters saturating at K_CBBD6 make the function wait for settling after transitions of bytes A56B and ACF0.
Helper 1CF46 returning 1 forces all outputs to 0, i.e. an inhibit/abort path.
fn-3162C.weakest_link: None of the input RAM variables other than ECT and RPM are identified, and neither are the helpers 22F92, 29BA4 and 1CF46. Calling this an OBD monitor enable, and saying which monitor it serves, therefore rests on the structure of the code rather than on any named signal.

fn-4AA58.mechanism: Reads the byte at 0xFFFF8EDC. If it is non-zero, it branches straight to 0x04AE62 (past the end of the listing, presumably the epilogue) and runs nothing. If it is zero, it zero-extends the byte argument r4 and saves it twice on the stack. It then calls about 90 subroutines one after another in a fixed order, from 0x22E36 and 0x1CF80 through 0x758CA. None of the return values are used. The saved argument is passed explicitly in r4 to 0x3043A, 0x30754 and 0x758CA; 0x22E36 also still has it in r4. Most of the other callees get no argument from this code. After the chain, 0x6F0B8 is called if the argument is 0 and also if the argument is 2, so once for either value. It then reads the byte at 0xFFFF8322; if that byte is zero it calls 0x3A8C8 and then 0x903EA. The listing stops there; the rest of the function (around 0x04AE48/0x04AE62) is not shown. Everything from 0x04ACB2 to 0x04AE2E is the literal pool of call targets, not code.
fn-4AA58.purpose: Most likely one of the engine computer's scheduler task routines: a fixed, ordered list of module update functions that runs each time the task is called. It can be suppressed by a global inhibit/mode flag at 0xFFFF8EDC. The byte argument looks like a slot or phase number that a few modules use, and that decides whether 0x6F0B8 runs (slots 0 and 2). A second flag at 0xFFFF8322 gates two further calls.
evidence: A long straight-line run of jsr calls through pooled function pointers, with no computation between them and no return values used, is the shape of a task-list dispatcher.
The whole list is skipped (bra 0x04AE62) when the byte at 0xFFFF8EDC is non-zero, so that byte is a global enable/inhibit for the list.
The argument is zero-extended from a byte, saved on the stack and re-loaded into r4 for a few specific callees only; it is compared against 0 and against 2 to decide whether 0x6F0B8 is called.
The byte at 0xFFFF8322 being zero gates the calls to 0x3A8C8 and 0x903EA.
None of the callees or RAM addresses carry verified names, so the meaning of each called module is not known.
fn-4AA58.weakest_link: The meanings of the argument (slot/phase number) and of the gate flags 0xFFFF8EDC and 0xFFFF8322 are not established by the code shown. Also, the function's tail after 0x04AE42, including the 0x04AE48 and 0x04AE62 paths, is cut off, so later behaviour may be missing.

fn-431B0.mechanism: Loads rpm_current (FFFF6624) into fr4, ect_current (FFFF6350) into fr15 and iat_current (FFFF6364) into fr14, then reads a state/counter byte at FFFF80C8. Branch 1: if that byte is unsigned-greater than the ROM byte at 0xD2988, it reads the float at FFFF80C4 (struct offset -4), adds the ROM float at 0xD2D10, passes the sum through float_min against 0.0 and writes the result back to FFFF80C4. The value therefore steps by a fixed amount each call and is capped at 0. Branch 2: otherwise, if the byte is unsigned >= the ROM byte at 0xD2987, it calls table_lookup_1D on table 0xADFC0. fr4 still holds RPM at that point, so the lookup is presumably on RPM. The result goes to FFFF80D0 (+8). It then calls table_lookup_2D on table 0xAE530 with ECT and IAT as the two axes and stores the result at FFFF80D4 (+12). It writes the product (FFFF80D0 × FFFF80D4) to FFFF80C4 and sets the byte at FFFF80CA (+2) to 1. Branch 3: if the byte is below 0xD2987, nothing is written. All three paths restore fr14, fr15 and pr and return.
fn-431B0.purpose: unknown. It computes a correction term at FFFF80C4 as f(RPM) × g(ECT,IAT) while a state/counter byte sits inside a calibrated window, and sets a 'computed' flag. Once the byte passes the upper threshold, the term is moved by a fixed step toward 0 and capped at 0. That fits a temperature-dependent compensation applied at an event (start or after-start, transition) that then decays away, but the actual quantity cannot be identified from this code.
evidence: rpm_current, ect_current and iat_current are read from the [VERIFIED-BOTH] addresses FFFF6624, FFFF6350 and FFFF6364
cmp/hi against ROM byte 0xD2988 selects the step-and-clamp path: float at FFFF80C4 + ROM float 0xD2D10, then float_min with fr5=0.0
cmp/hs against ROM byte 0xD2987 gates the table path

table_lookup_2D on table 0xAE530 is called with fr4=ECT, fr5=IAT; its result is stored at FFFF80D4
FFFF80D0*FFFF80D4 is stored to FFFF80C4, and byte FFFF80CA is set to 1
The listing after 0x043228 (pushes of r12-r14) is the start of the next function
fn-431B0.weakest_link: The meaning of the state/counter byte at FFFF80C8 and of the output at FFFF80C4 is not shown; it is also assumed that table_lookup_1D takes its input in fr4, so that the 1D axis is RPM. As a result the purpose (e.g. after-start or transient compensation) is not supported by this code alone.

fn-52092.mechanism:
Saves FPU and GBR state, then sets GBR to 0xFFFF8998. It snapshots RAM inputs onto the stack: rpm_current (fr12), floats at 0xFFFF65FC (fr15), 6634, 6628 (fr14), 8AE4, 87CC, 87AC, 8B14 and 895C (fr13), the word at 67EC, and status bytes at 65BF, 8A74, 5BE3, 5BE2, 65C0, 7C9D, 5FB6, 5FB7, 6254 and 85D7. It also stores the results of two helper calls, 0x2F8EA and 0x22CF4.

It then updates a set of saturating uint16 condition-duration timers in the GBR block, each stepped with uint16_add_sat(x,1):
- +104 counts while byte 5BE2==1 and resets otherwise.
- +106 counts while 65BF==1 and resets otherwise; +108 counts in the opposite state.
- +110 counts while 5BE3==0.
- +116 counts while the 0x22CF4 result is 0.
- +112 counts while 65C0==0; +114 counts in the opposite state.

It also maintains latched flags:
- +120 is set when the 0x2F8EA result is 0 and rpm >= value@895C; it is cleared when that result is nonzero.
- +121 and +122 are latched when rpm >= value@6628 + const@D658C; they are cleared under the same condition as +120.
- +123 is a hysteresis flag on the float at 65FC: set when it is >= cal D6598, cleared when it is < cal D6594.

Next it gates on word 8912 == cal D6218 and byte 8910 == 1; otherwise it branches out of the listing. It takes a 1D table lookup on rpm (table 0xAEFB4 or 0xAEFA8, chosen by the 0x22CF4 result) and keeps a second value from D65A0 or D659C. It clamps the float at 0xFFFF89F8 (8A10-24) to cal D6590 when 65BF==0, latching a local flag. It runs float_deadband_check on 0xFFFF88EC.

Finally it walks a long AND-chain of enable conditions. Each timer must exceed its calibration (D622E, D6230, D6232, D6234, D6236, D6238, D623A), some only when that calibration is nonzero. The 5FB6 and 5FB7 bytes must not be 1. The word at 67EC must be >= cal D623C, the value at 65FC must be < cal D6588, and the bytes at 6254/85D7 and flag +122 are checked. Any failure branches to 0x05249A. The listing is cut off before the success and failure stores.
fn-52092.purpose: Most likely the enable-condition evaluator for an OBD diagnostic monitor: it debounces the required operating conditions over time (rpm windows, temperature- or load-like floats, status flags), and only when all have held for their calibrated durations does it allow the monitor or test to run. Which monitor this is cannot be told from the code shown.
evidence: Repeated pattern of reset-to-0 / uint16_add_sat(+1) on GBR words 104-116, keyed on status bytes, is the classic condition-hold timer
Each timer is later compared with a uint16 calibration in 0xD622E-0xD623A; any failure jumps to a common exit at 0x05249A
Hysteresis flag +123 uses two calibrations (D6598 set, D6594 clear) on the float at 65FC
rpm (VERIFIED) is compared against an RAM threshold and a threshold plus an offset to latch flags +120, +121 and +122
Up-front gating on word 8912 == cal D6218 and byte 8910 == 1, followed by an rpm-indexed table_lookup_1D
fn-52092.weakest_link: None of the input RAM addresses other than rpm is identified, and the listing ends before the outcome at 0x05249A and the success path is written. The specific monitor, and even whether the result is an enable flag, is unconfirmed.

fn-4A94C.mechanism: Reads the byte at RAM 0xFFFF8EDC. If it is non-zero the function returns at once and does nothing. If it is zero, it zero-extends the byte argument r4 and keeps it in a stack slot. It then calls a fixed list of subroutines in order: 0x43750, 0x22DB0, 0x23286, 0x2EF3C, 0x2FA84, 0x2FC5C, 0x2FD42, 0x2F974, 0x33304, 0x32B10, 0x31D1E, 0x3297A, 0x31A6A, 0x39820, 0x3C392, 0x3E8DC, 0x758C4, 0x3D552, 0x3D68C, 0x3D856, 0x3D648, 0x46C68 and 0x471E8. It ends with a tail jump to 0x22F8A. The saved argument is reloaded into r4 in a delay slot before the calls to 0x22DB0, 0x758C4, 0x3D856, 0x46C68 and 0x471E8. Because 0x43750 is called with the original r4 still in place, it may receive it too. Whether the remaining callees, including the tail callee 0x22F8A, use whatever is left in r4 cannot be told from this code. The function computes nothing and stores nothing itself; it only sequences calls.
fn-4A94C.purpose: Most likely one periodic scheduler slot (a time-sliced task list) that runs a batch of engine-control subsystem routines in a fixed order. It forwards a byte parameter, possibly a tick or phase index, to some of them. The whole batch is suppressed while the flag byte at 0xFFFF8EDC is set. That flag could be an init-in-progress, inhibit or busy marker. Its exact meaning and the jobs of the callees are unknown from this listing.
evidence: mov.b @r2,r5 / tst r5,r5 / bf 0x04A9EC: a non-zero byte at 0xFFFF8EDC skips everything and goes to rts
There are 23 jsr calls through literal-pool addresses with no logic between them, which is a pure call sequencer
mov.l r4,@r15 saves the extu.b argument; mov.l @r15,r4 in delay slots reloads it for 0x22DB0, 0x758C4, 0x3D856, 0x46C68 and 0x471E8; 0x43750 is called while the original r4 is still in place
The last call is a tail call: jmp @r2 to 0x22F8A with lds.l @r15+,pr in the delay slot
Bytes from 0x04A9F4 on are the literal pool (call targets), not code
fn-4A94C.weakest_link: The scheduler-slot interpretation and the meanings of the r4 parameter and the 0xFFFF8EDC flag are not shown. No callee was examined, and the caller that supplies r4 is not visible.

fn-3FA8C.mechanism: Saves PR and GBR, then sets GBR to 0xFFFF7EC0 and r5 to 0xFFFF7EFC. Loads ect_current (0xFFFF6350) into fr4. Loads a float literal from 0x03FB84 (value not shown) and stores it to 0xFFFF7ECC (r5-48), 0xFFFF7EC0 (r5-60) and 0xFFFF7EC4 (r5-56). Loads a second float literal from 0x03FB94 and stores it to 0xFFFF7EDC (r5-32). Puts -1 in r0 and stores 0xFFFF as words at GBR+60 (0xFFFF7EFC) and GBR+62 (0xFFFF7EFE). In the jsr delay slot it stores 0xFF as a byte at GBR+40 (0xFFFF7EE8). It calls table_lookup_1D with r4 = 0x000ADA98 (a table descriptor) and ECT in fr4, and stores the float result fr0 to 0xFFFF7EE4 (r5-24). It then restores GBR and PR and returns. The instructions after rts/nop at 0x03FACE belong to the next function.
fn-3FA8C.purpose: Most likely a one-shot initializer or reset routine for the state block at 0xFFFF7EC0-0xFFFF7EFF. It writes fixed defaults to several float variables and 0xFFFF/0xFF markers to word and byte variables, which look like 'not yet set' sentinels or counters. It seeds one variable (0xFFFF7EE4) from an ECT-indexed 1D table, presumably a coolant-temperature-dependent starting value. Which subsystem owns this block cannot be told from this code.
evidence: GBR is set to 0xFFFF7EC0 and every store targets 0xFFFF7EC0..0xFFFF7EFE, so one contiguous RAM block is being written.
The routine only writes: constants, -1 sentinels, and one table result. Nothing is read back or compared, which is the shape of an initialization routine.
fr4 is loaded from ect_current [VERIFIED-BOTH] right before table_lookup_1D [TRACED] is called with descriptor 0x000ADA98, so the lookup is ECT-indexed.
The byte store at GBR+40 sits in the jsr delay slot and runs before the call.
The function has no inputs besides ECT and no conditional branches.
fn-3FA8C.weakest_link: The float literals at 0x03FB84 and 0x03FB94 and the contents of table 0x000ADA98 are not shown, and none of the target RAM addresses are named. 'Init/reset of a subsystem' rests on the code's structure, not on any identified variable, and the owning subsystem is unknown.

fn-0CB88.mechanism: This is a leaf-style wrapper that makes four calls to the helper at 0x00CC80, always with r6 = 0. Because of the delay slots, the argument triples (r4, r5, r6) are: (0, 0x00A4, 0), then (0, 0x00A8, 0), then (1, 0x00A4, 0), then (1, 0x00A8, 0). In the first two calls r4 is set from r6 (= 0) in the bsr delay slot. The last call is a tail call: bra 0x00CC80 with PR restored in the delay slot. The function itself reads no memory except the two 16-bit constants in its literal pool (0x00A4 at 0xCBFA and 0x00A8 at 0xCBFC). It computes nothing and stores nothing directly; every effect happens inside 0x00CC80.
fn-0CB88.purpose: Unknown. The structure looks like initialisation or reset: the same pair of offsets or IDs (0xA4, 0xA8) is set to value 0 for two instances or channels (index 0 and 1). The meaning of 0xA4/0xA8 and what 0x00CC80 writes to cannot be determined from this listing.
evidence: Four calls to 0x00CC80. The first argument (r4) is 0, 0, 1, 1, set in the bsr delay slots or just before the final bra.
The second argument (r5) alternates between literals 0x00A4 and 0x00A8.
The third argument (r6) is always 0.
The final call is a tail call (bra with lds.l @r15+,pr in the delay slot), so the helper's return value is passed back to the caller.
There are no loads or stores to RAM or registers in this function itself.
fn-0CB88.weakest_link: The 'observed' class covers only the mechanism. Any purpose depends on what 0x00CC80 does with (index, 0xA4/0xA8, 0), and that helper is not shown. Reading it as per-channel peripheral or register initialisation is a hunch.

fn-0E774.mechanism: Saves PR. Reads SR, clears the interrupt-mask field (AND 0xFF0F) and ORs in 0xF0, so the IMASK level becomes 15 and maskable interrupts are blocked. It pushes the incoming r4 to the stack, but that slot is only discarded later and never read back. It moves the caller's argument into r5, loads r4 = 0x4000 and calls 0x00010800(r4=0x4000, r5=arg). Afterwards it drops the pushed word (add #4,r15), restores PR in the jmp delay slot and tail-jumps to 0x0000FBA4. Whatever registers 0x10800 leaves, probably including its return value in r0, pass through to that routine. The function itself never saves or restores the old SR value.
fn-0E774.purpose: Likely a small atomic wrapper: with interrupts disabled, it runs helper 0x10800 on constant 0x4000 (perhaps a bit mask, an ID or a size) and the caller's argument. It then hands off to 0xFBA4, which probably re-enables or restores interrupts and finishes the operation. The exact meaning of 0x4000 and of the two callees is unknown from this listing.
evidence: stc sr / and 0xFF0F / or #240 / ldc r0,sr sets IMASK to 0xF, disabling maskable interrupts (observed)
r5 = original r4 and r4 = 0x4000 (mov.w, positive, no sign-extension issue) before jsr 0x00010800 (observed)
The pushed r4 is discarded via add #4,r15 and never reloaded (observed)
jmp @0x0000FBA4 with lds.l @r15+,pr in the delay slot is a tail call (observed)
SR is not restored locally, so 0xFBA4 presumably restores interrupts (inferred)
fn-0E774.weakest_link: The roles of 0x10800 and 0xFBA4 are not shown. In particular, that 0xFBA4 re-enables interrupts and what 0x4000 means (mask, ID, length) are unverified.

fn-3EB8C.mechanism: Reads the byte at 0xFFFF65BD. If it is nonzero, it writes 0 to the byte at 0xFFFF7E8C and 0 to the u16 at 0xFFFF7E8E (struct base+2). If it is zero, it reads the u16 counter at 0xFFFF7E8E and compares it unsigned (cmp/hs) against the u16 ROM constant at 0x000D29AA. When counter >= constant it sets the byte 0xFFFF7E8C to 1; otherwise it leaves that byte unchanged, so the flag latches. It then calls uint16_add_sat(counter, 1) and stores the result back to 0xFFFF7E8E, a saturating increment. It ends with a tail jump to 0x00046BCC, restoring pr in the delay slot.
fn-3EB8C.purpose: A generic elapsed-time or debounce timer. While the condition byte 0xFFFF65BD is zero, a saturating counter runs once per call. Once it reaches the calibration threshold at 0xD29AA, a 'time elapsed' flag at 0xFFFF7E8C is latched to 1. Both counter and flag reset whenever 0xFFFF65BD becomes nonzero. What the condition and the flag mean in engine terms is unknown from this code.
evidence: mov.b @0xFFFF65BD; tst; bf -> when nonzero, mov #0 and stores to @0xFFFF7E8C (byte) and @(2,0xFFFF7E8C) (word)
Zero path: mov.w @(2,r1) counter compared with mov.w @0x000D29AA via cmp/hs (unsigned >=); when true, mov #1 -> mov.b @0xFFFF7E8C
jsr uint16_add_sat [TRACED] with r4=extu.w counter and r5=1 (set in the delay slot); the result r0 is stored by mov.w r0,@(2,r1)
The flag is only set, never cleared, on the zero path, so it latches until the reset path runs
0x000D29AA is a ROM address, so the threshold is a calibration constant
Ends with jmp 0x00046BCC (tail call), pr restored in the delay slot
fn-3EB8C.weakest_link: The mechanism is fully fixed by the code. Only the physical meaning of 0xFFFF65BD, 0xFFFF7E8C and the threshold is unknown, as is what the tail-called 0x46BCC does; the call rate (time units) is not shown.

fn-31C9C.mechanism: Calls the helper at 0x22F92 and zero-extends its byte return. The byte at 0xFFFF94B3 is always loaded into r1, because the load sits in the branch delay slot. If the return is not 1, the function exits without writing anything. If it is 1: (1) writes 1.0f to 0xFFFF76D4 (0x7700-44) and 0xFFFF76FC (0x7700-4). (2) Zeroes 42 floats at 0xFFFF74C8..0xFFFF756F. (3) Zeroes 42 floats at 0xFFFF757C..0xFFFF7623. (4) Zeroes 41 floats at 0xFFFF7630..0xFFFF76D3, which ends directly at the 1.0f slot 0xFFFF76D4. (5) Writes 1.0f to 0xFFFF76D8 and 0xFFFF76DC. (6) Copies the byte from 0xFFFF94B3 into 0xFFFF7701. (7) Clears the bytes 0xFFFF7702 and 0xFFFF76E0 to 0.
fn-31C9C.purpose: Re-initialises one RAM block of a subsystem: three float arrays (42/42/41 entries) are reset to 0.0, several scale/factor floats are reset to 1.0, and a state byte is reseeded from 0xFFFF94B3. This is done only when the predicate at 0x22F92 returns 1, most plausibly a reset, init or 'conditions changed' request. The subsystem itself (learning/adaptation, filter history or other) cannot be identified from this code.
evidence: bf/s 0x031D18 after cmp/eq #1,r0 on the zero-extended return of jsr 0x22F92 gates all writes

fn-0DE38.mechanism: First calls 0x10A46 with r4=3. Then it loops. Each pass calls critical_section_enter(r4=&stack slot, r5=0xE0); 0xE0 looks like an SR interrupt-mask value. Inside the critical section it calls 0xF97C(r4=2, r5=0xFFFF4548), keeps the return value in r12, and reads the byte at 0xFFFF4578 (0xFFFF4576+2) into r13. It then calls critical_section_exit with the saved word at @r15. If r12==0, it loads the function pointer stored at 0xFFFF4548 and calls it with r4=0xFFFF454C (the struct base + 4). It repeats while the byte read from 0xFFFF4578 is non-zero. When that byte is zero it calls 0x35A4 once and returns. It does not save r8-r14, which is unusual for an ordinary SH callee.
fn-0DE38.purpose: Most likely an RTOS-style task or service loop. It repeatedly asks a kernel or queue routine (0xF97C, op/ID 2) about the control block at 0xFFFF4548. On a zero (ready/success) result it invokes that block's stored handler pointer with a pointer to the block's payload at +4. It keeps going while a continue/pending flag at 0xFFFF4578 is set, then calls a closing or yield routine (0x35A4). What the handler actually does at the engine level is unknown.

fn-4530A.mechanism: It loads float A from 0xFFFF8584, current RPM from 0xFFFF6624, and a ROM calibration float C from 0x000D2E78. Each time this happens the stored RPM is overwritten, so it holds the RPM from the last call where A was at or above C. If A < C, it reads the uint16 counter at 0xFFFF8226. If the counter is 0xFFFF it resets it to 0. If it is 0xFFFE or more it leaves it alone. Otherwise it adds 1 through uint16_add_sat(counter,1) and stores the result. Net effect: 0xFFFF8226 is a call-count timer of how long A has been below C, using 0xFFFF as an 'active/reset' sentinel and saturating at 0xFFFE. 0xFFFF820C holds the RPM latched while A was still at or above C.

fn-41A7E.mechanism:

- If A == 1 and C != 1: when B != 1, state 2. When B == 1, counter(+12) >= cal u16 0xD29CA gives state 1. Below that count, state 1 if 0xD2C24 <= fr8, else the previous state is held.

- State 1: acc = float_min(acc + table_lookup_1D(table 0xAE17C, rpm), 0.0).
- State 2: the same, using table 0xAE170.
- State 3: acc = cal float 0xD2C28.
- State 0: acc = 0.0.

fn-040DE.mechanism: GBR is set to 0xFFFF4024. The same sequence runs three times, for the three A/D converter blocks at 0xFFFFF818/9, 0xFFFFF838/9 and 0xFFFFF858/9, each inside a critical_section_enter/exit pair (r5=0xE0, saved state kept in the 12-byte stack frame). Each sequence does four things: (1) it clears bit 5 of the control byte at base+1 (ADCR, the ADST start bit), stopping the converter; (2) it reads the status byte at base (ADCSR), which is the read-before-clear for ADF; (3) it writes a new ADCSR value: 0x33 for converters 0 and 1, 0x2B for converter 2; (4) it sets ADCR = (ADCR & 0x2F) | 0x20, which starts conversion. Outside the critical sections it writes three bytes: 2 to 0xFFFF40A4 (GBR+128), 0 to 0xFFFF40A9 (GBR+133) and 0xFF to 0xFFFF40AA (GBR+134). It then busy-waits, one converter after another, until bit 7 (ADF, conversion end) of each ADCSR is set. Finally it copies 32 16-bit result registers into RAM: 0xFFFFF800-0xFFFFF816 (ADDR0-11) to 0xFFFF4024-0xFFFF403A; 0xFFFFF820-0xFFFFF836 (ADDR12-23) to 0xFFFF403C-0xFFFF4052; 0xFFFFF840-0xFFFFF84E (ADDR24-31) to 0xFFFF4054-0xFFFF4062. fn-717B2.mechanism: Reads the byte counter at 0xFFFF979D and compares it, as unsigned 8-bit values, with the byte argument r4. If they are equal, it calls uint8_add_sat(counter, 1) and stores the saturated result back to 0xFFFF979D. If they differ, it stores 0xFF to 0xFFFF979D. A value of 0xFF then sticks: a later match needs r4 = 0xFF, and a saturating add on 0xFF stays 0xFF. The function returns nothing. The listing runs past the rts into a neighbouring routine at 0x0717DA. That routine loads r5 = 0xFFFF9795 and reads the same counter at r5+8 (= 0xFFFF979D). It compares the counter with 25, writes the byte (counter != 25) to 0xFFFF9795, and resets the counter to 0.

The counter advances only if the checkpoints run in order; any out-of-order call latches it to 0xFF. The neighbouring routine then checks once per cycle that exactly 25 checkpoints ran in order. It sets an error flag at 0xFFFF9795 if not, and restarts the sequence.

On a mismatch the constant 0xFF (mov #-1) is written to 0xFFFF979D. It acts as a sticky invalid marker, because saturation keeps it at 0xFF.
The neighbour at 0x0717DA reads @(8, 0xFFFF9795), which is the same address 0xFFFF979D. It compares that with 25, stores the inverted equality result to 0xFFFF9795 as a flag, and zeroes the counter.
No other state is touched, and nothing is returned.

The callers are not shown, and neither the counter nor the flag at 0xFFFF9795 has a verified name.
